instruction.text: Look at the emotion and decide which situations could make someone feel that way. Choose two situations.

b: ++His classmate stole the ball he was playing with at breaktime.
His parents packed him a delicious lunch.
++His teacher blamed him for something his classmate did.
++He wasn’t picked last for the teams in PE.
++He didn’t have any homework for today.
He had to stay after school to clean up the mess he made.
He helped his classmate answer a tough question.
++He tripped and fell in front of his class.
++He farted during reading time.
++Nobody wants to play the game she suggested at breaktime.
++Her neighbour didn’t come to school today, so she sat alone in class all day.
After school, all her siblings were home, and she couldn’t watch her favourite show.
++She talked to the new girl during class for the first time.
She failed her music test and will have to try again.
++She let another child have a turn batting in rounders and took a break.
++She is practising her solo in front of the class.
++She is trying a new game at breaktime.
She is playing with her dog at home.
++Their class misbehaved, and now they are missing golden time.
++They keep making mistakes while playing football at breaktime.
The class is having a pizza party because they read so many books.
She got caught running in the hallway at school.
++She won each of the games she played at breaktime.
++Her class donated the most books, and they won the competition.
